title: How do we sort expressions without working them out?
description: Six expressions are made from two hundred forty five point zero five, zero point nine four two three six eight and seven point nine six eight two. The video sorts them from smallest to biggest by asking whether a number is below or above one, and not by exact working.
teaching_notes: One idea: multiplying or dividing by a number below one or above one tells which way the result moves, so a rough size is enough to sort. Ask the class whether dividing by a number below one makes a result bigger or smaller before any work is shown. Watch for students who think dividing always makes a number smaller.

source: End of chapter Figure it Out, Q11
video_script.why: The child has used a nearby whole number fact to place the decimal point, and now rounds the decimals to nearby numbers to see which way each result moves.
video_script.substitution: The decimals are replaced by nearby numbers, about one and about eight, and the direction of each result is read from whether the multiplier or divisor is below or above one.
video_script.anchor: Six expressions from 245.05, 0.942368 and 7.9682 listed with their letters, to be sorted in increasing order
video_script.payoff_line: From smallest to biggest, the order is sixth, third, first, fifth, fourth, second

final_answer.spoken: from smallest to biggest, the order is sixth, third, first, fifth, fourth, second

maths_rules: 0.942368 is below 1 and close to 1: 245.05 x 0.942368 is a little under 245.05 (about 231); 245.05 / 0.942368 is a little over 245.05 (about 260)
7.9682 is near 8: 245.05 x 7.9682 is about 245.05 x 8, about 1960 (exactly about 1952.6); 245.05 / 7.9682 is about 245.05 / 8, about 31 (exactly about 30.75)
video_script.design: One idea: read the direction of each result from whether the number is below or above one. The six expressions stay on the board all video; the working band compares with the middle number, then with about eight, then sorts the smaller ones and the bigger ones.
open_questions: The video names the six expressions by their order in the list (first to sixth), since the letters cannot be spoken safely. The list on the board shows the letters beside each expression.
